question.text: In a harmonic progression <math><msub><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><msub><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><msub><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo></math> it is given that <math><msub><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>50.</mn></math> If <math><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></math> denotes the sum of first <math><mi>n</mi></math> terms of this, then the value of <math><mi>n</mi></math> for which <math><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></math> is maximum is

solution.text:
Let the first term be a and the common difference be d, then

 20=1a+4d and 50=1a+5d
On solving, we get,

 d=-3100 and a=17100
Hence, tr=10020-3r>0⇒r<203⇒rmax=6
So, sum is maximum for n=6, as after this terms are negative
